From c0e310188299358279fc27c88512f94db78991a6 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Chris Wilson <chris@chris-wilson.co.uk>
Date: Thu, 27 Feb 2020 08:57:04 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] drm/i915: Skip barriers inside waits

Attaching to the i915_active barrier is a two stage process, and a flush
is only effective when the barrier is activation. Thus it is possible
for us to see a barrier, and attempt to flush, only for our flush to
have no effect. As such, before attempting to activate signaling on the
fence we need to double check it is a fence!

Fixes: d13a31770077 ("drm/i915: Flush idle barriers when waiting")
Closes: https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/drm/intel/issues/1333
Signed-off-by: Chris Wilson <chris@chris-wilson.co.uk>
Cc: Tvrtko Ursulin <tvrtko.ursulin@intel.com>
Reviewed-by: Andi Shyti <andi.shyti@intel.com>
Link: https://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/msgid/20200227085723.1961649-1-chris@chris-wilson.co.uk

diff --git a/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_active.c b/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_active.c
index 0b12d5023800..7b3d6c12ad61 100644
--- a/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_active.c
+++ b/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_active.c
@@ -453,6 +453,9 @@ static void enable_signaling(struct i915_active_fence *active)
 {
 	struct dma_fence *fence;
 
+	if (unlikely(is_barrier(active)))
+		return;
+
 	fence = i915_active_fence_get(active);
 	if (!fence)
 		return;
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_active.c`**
   - A new check was added at the beginning of the `enable_signaling` function to determine if the `active` object is a barrier using the `is_barrier(active)` function.
   - If the object is identified as a barrier, the function returns early, effectively skipping the signaling activation process for barriers.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modification in `i915_active.c` addresses a specific issue related to the handling of barriers in the i915 driver. By adding a check to skip the signaling activation for barriers, the patch ensures that unnecessary flush attempts are avoided, which could lead to ineffective operations. This change is a direct response to the identified bug in the previous implementation (referenced by the fix tag), enhancing the robustness of the barrier handling mechanism in the driver.

Here is the commit message:
drm/i915: Skip barriers inside waits

Attaching to the i915_active barrier is a two stage process, and a flush
is only effective when the barrier is activation. Thus it is possible
for us to see a barrier, and attempt to flush, only for our flush to
have no effect. As such, before attempting to activate signaling on the
fence we need to double check it is a fence!

Fixes: d13a31770077 ("drm/i915: Flush idle barriers when waiting")
Closes: https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/drm/intel/issues/1333
Signed-off-by: Chris Wilson <chris@chris-wilson.co.uk>
Cc: Tvrtko Ursulin <tvrtko.ursulin@intel.com>
Reviewed-by: Andi Shyti <andi.shyti@intel.com>
Link: https://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/msgid/20200227085723.1961649-1-chris@chris-wilson.co.uk

Here is the root cause:
The bug arises from the incorrect handling of barriers in the i915 driver, where an attempt to flush a barrier could occur even when the barrier is not activated. This could lead to ineffective flush operations, as the flush is only meaningful when the barrier is in an active state. The lack of a prior check to confirm whether the object is a barrier allows for this erroneous behavior.

Here is the patch:
 
 static void enable_signaling(struct i915_active_fence *active)
 {
 	struct dma_fence *fence;
 
+	if (unlikely(is_barrier(active)))
+		return;
+
 	fence = i915_active_fence_get(active);
 	if (!fence)
 		return;
 
 	dma_fence_enable_sw_signaling(fence);
 	dma_fence_put(fence);
 }

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
fence = i915_active_fence_get(active);
dma_fence_enable_sw_signaling(fence);
```
Reason:
The bug occurs because the code attempts to flush a barrier without first confirming whether the barrier is activated. The `i915_active_fence_get(active)` function retrieves the fence associated with the active barrier, and the subsequent call to `dma_fence_enable_sw_signaling(fence)` attempts to enable signaling on that fence. If the barrier is not activated, this operation is ineffective, leading to potential issues in the driver.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if (unlikely(is_barrier(active)))
    return;
```
Reason:
The fix introduces a check to determine if the active object is a barrier before proceeding with the signaling operation. By using `is_barrier(active)`, the code can skip the signaling process if the object is indeed a barrier, thus preventing ineffective flush operations and ensuring that signaling is only attempted on valid, activated fences.
